explanation: Changing a real type or mode can replace the old configuration and initialize the new one with defaults. This pattern matches a report that assumes settings from the inactive mode must survive, although review accepts their replacement; examples include changing a form-field type, a webhook method or the selected issue-tracker mode. Verify that a genuine mode change occurred and what preservation is promised. Reselecting the same mode while secretly resetting values, or ignoring settings still saved for the active mode, is outside this rejection.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Start signed in as the admin account using the provided saved authentication state; no credentials were entered. Open /discounts/vouchers?asc=true&sort=code. Create a fresh voucher named vouchers-7q4p-20260613. Add the manual code VOUCHERS-20260613-K8Q2, assign Channel-USD, select Entire order and Percentage, enter 10%, and save. On the created voucher at /discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlcjoxMQ%3D%3D, open Requirements, enable Minimal order value, enter 50 for Channel-USD, and save. Verify the toggle is on and the amount displays as 50.00 USD. Enable Minimum quantity of items. Observe that Minimal order value is now off and its amount field is absent, while Minimum quantity of items is on. Save the change, refresh the voucher page, and reopen Requirements. Confirm Minimal order value remains off and Minimum quantity of items remains on. The rejected report expected: The separately presented optional thresholds remain enabled together: the $50.00 Channel-USD minimum order value remains active when Minimum quantity of items is enabled. It claimed this outcome: With Minimal order value enabled and saved at $50.00, enabling Minimum quantity of items immediately turned Minimal order value off and removed its amount field. After saving and refreshing, Minimal order value remained off while Minimum quantity of items remained on. Review concluded: Human review rejected the reported expectation as inconsistent with intended behavior. The pre-redesign voucher UI used a radio group with NONE, ORDER and ITEM choices, and the pinned E2E tests exercise choosing one requirement type at a time. The redesign preserves that selection model with button-like controls. Therefore switching to minimum item quantity replacing minimum order value is consistent with established dashboard interaction design. Core voucher APIs can represent both fields, so this conclusion is about dashboard behavior rather than an API restriction.

explanation: An announcement, dropdown or active text editor can cover a button or consume the first click meant for another command. In the reviewed cases, dismissing that layer, finishing the edit, or clicking again after it closes makes the requested action work. This pattern matches a report that calls the covered command broken without completing that supported first step or establishing a requirement for one click to both dismiss and activate. It does not cover a layer that cannot be dismissed, edits lost during dismissal, or a command that still fails afterward.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the authorized Saleor dashboard admin using the supplied saved authentication state (no credentials or saved-state path included). In the dashboard, create a disposable voucher with a manual code, Channel-USD, Entire order / Percentage at 10%, and a QA name; save it and open its detail page. In a fresh authenticated browser session at 414×896, navigate to /discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlcjo2. With the default Saleor Pulse announcement open, change Voucher Name and scroll to the bottom so Save is enabled. Click the center of Save while Pulse remains open. The edit does not save; after dismissing Pulse, Save remains available. Click Save again and verify the update completes and the edited name is visible. Repeat in a fresh authenticated browser session at 390×844 on the same voucher detail page: change Voucher Name, scroll to the bottom, and click the center of enabled Save with Pulse open. The edit does not complete. Dismiss Pulse and click Save; the control transitions through saving and then becomes disabled. This confirms recovery, not that the first click saved. The rejected report expected: With the voucher Save control enabled, clicking its center should save the edited voucher rather than have the click intercepted by the promotional announcement. It claimed this outcome: At 414×896 and 390×844, the open Pulse panel covered most of the fixed Save control. A center click produced no save; the edit remained pending. After dismissing Pulse, Save worked and the edited name was visible. Review concluded: Human review rejected the claim that this dismissible announcement overlap is a voucher Save bug. The supplied reproduction shows an open promotional announcement partially intercepting Save; its accessible Dismiss Pulse announcement control works, and Save succeeds after dismissal. Dismissing the announcement is the expected way to reveal the covered control. The record does not establish an undismissable overlay, a broken Save after dismissal, or a requirement that the announcement remain open while saving. This rejection is limited to the reported open-announcement overlap with mobile voucher Save and does not classify other Pulse interactions.

explanation: A report's specific factual claim is contradicted by a decisive observation or by a controlled repetition of the same setup. For example, the allegedly deleted value is still present, or the allegedly broken control performs the requested action when activated as described. Match this pattern only when that counterevidence addresses the same value, action and conditions; a vaguely similar successful workflow is insufficient. The finding rejects the checked allegation, not every related defect or every possible historical failure.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Create and save a disposable Products voucher with a unique code, an assigned sales channel, a positive percentage discount, and Monospace Tee S (SKU 328223580) assigned as an eligible variant. Switch to Free shipping, save, and reload the saved detail. Switch back to Products, enter a positive percentage, and save. Open Assign variants and search the sibling SKU 328223581. Inspect the existing Monospace Tee S (SKU 328223580): the report claims it is unchecked and selectable and can be assigned again. Compare the resulting assigned count with the unique visible rows. The rejected report expected: Already assigned variants remain checked and disabled in the assignment picker, and the assigned count matches the unique eligible variants. It claimed this outcome: The report claimed that the existing Monospace Tee S could be selected again after the type roundtrip, producing 2 assigned with only one S row; Save then normalized the count to 1. Review concluded: User-approved rejection as reported after independent Mo and Codex browser checks did not reproduce it. Mo checked the Channel-PLN roundtrip; Codex independently checked Channel-USD. In both, the existing S variant remained checked and disabled, Assign stayed disabled without a new selection, and closing the picker left one assigned variant and one visible row. The pinned picker explicitly locks already assigned IDs. This rejection is scoped to the supplied roundtrip and duplicate-selection claim; it does not establish that every timing, channel or eligibility-state variant is impossible.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers. Create a disposable voucher with a unique name and manual code, assign Channel-USD, set a valid 10% discount, and set Start Date to 01/01/2030. Save and confirm its details show Scheduled. Return to All vouchers, open Filters, and select Status / is / Scheduled. Click Apply and inspect the list. Reopen Filters and repeat the selection and Apply; the report claims Active rows remain, the scheduled voucher is omitted, and the condition disappears. The rejected report expected: Applying Status is Scheduled should show scheduled vouchers, including the newly created future voucher, and exclude Active vouchers. It claimed this outcome: The report claims the filter panel closed while the list remained unfiltered with Active rows and no scheduled voucher; reopening Filters showed a blank condition, and repeating selection and Apply produced the same result. Review concluded: Human review rejected this reported failure as a hallucination. Independent verification on the pinned fixture showed the Scheduled condition persisted in the URL, query request, and reopened filter panel. The resulting list included the independently created future voucher and excluded Active and Ended vouchers. Applying the filter and retaining its condition worked correctly; the report’s alleged unfiltered list and lost condition were contradicted by the verified UI behavior.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Open /discounts/vouchers and open 'Big order discount'. Turn on 'Limit number of times this discount can be used in total' (value defaults to 1). Click the Limit of Uses input, press Ctrl+A then Backspace: the field shows 1 instead of being empty. Type 5: the field shows 15. Do the same with 'Minimum quantity of items' and type 3: it shows 13. Save and reload: usage limit 15 and min quantity 13 are saved. The rejected report expected: Clearing the field leaves it empty (or checks it only on blur/save), so select-all + type '5' gives 5. It claimed this outcome: After Ctrl+A + Backspace the value is instantly '1'; typing '5' then gives '15'. Saving sent usageLimit '15' and minCheckoutItemsQuantity 13, and both persisted after reload. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: clearing the field and typing a new value saves the new value.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Open /discounts/vouchers/add. Enter Voucher Name 'X'. Click Add code > Manual code. Type the unique code 'UNIQ456' and click Confirm. The dialog stays open showing 'Code already exists'. Click Back: the table lists UNIQ456 once and the checklist says '2 codes ready'. The rejected report expected: A unique code is added once and the dialog closes without an error. It claimed this outcome: The dialog stays open, the input is marked red with 'Code already exists', and the code (e.g. UNIQ456) already appears in the Voucher codes table. The checklist reads '2 codes ready'. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: confirming a unique code adds it once and closes the dialog.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Open Vouchers. Click Create voucher without assigning any channels. Read Availability. The rejected report expected: Availability summary reports no assigned channels. It claimed this outcome: Availability says Voucher in 2 of 2 channels while the card immediately below says No channels assigned and setup remains 0 of 3. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: an untouched Create Voucher form shows 0 of 2 channels with No channels assigned.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Open the voucher list as an authenticated administrator and clear any applied filters. Open Filters and configure Status is Expired without clicking Apply. Click Add condition. Inspect the filter panel. The rejected report expected: The configured condition row is retained and a second condition row is added. It claimed this outcome: The configured condition fields are reset to empty placeholders and no additional condition row is added. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: a completed filter condition survives Add condition; only unfinished rows are removed.

On a Saleor voucher with a saved minimum order value in one sales channel, add or re-add another channel and leave its new minimum amount blank. The rejected report claims Save shows Voucher updated but retains Unsaved changes: Channels. Human review instead observed a field-validation error when clearing the minimum value, so that successful-save allegation was not established. Keep the remove/save/re-add setup when checking an equivalent report; this does not reject a separately demonstrated successful save that retains dirty state.

explanation: An input can visibly change unsupported characters, dates or numeric precision while the user is still editing. This pattern matches a report that remembers the intended text and blames Save for a different result, although the field or preview already displayed that effective value before submission and the save preserved it. Observe the value immediately before saving and compare it with storage. A valid displayed value secretly replaced only during submission is a different failure.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in to the supplied Saleor fixture through its supported authentication setup and open Discounts > Vouchers. Create and save a disposable entire-order percentage voucher with a baseline code and Channel-USD. Open Codes > Add code > Generate codes. Starting with an empty Code Quantity, type the keys 1, decimal point, and 5 sequentially. Enter a unique code prefix. Observe that Code Quantity visibly reads 15 before confirming. Confirm and observe fifteen local Draft code rows with Unsaved changes: Codes; use pagination to inspect the remaining rows. For the related alias, reopen Generate codes with an empty quantity and type minus followed by 1 sequentially. Observe quantity 1 before Confirm and one additional local Draft code afterward. Discard the generated Draft codes through Vouchers > Ignore changes. The generated codes remain local and unsaved during the reported flow. The rejected report expected: A fractional quantity should be rejected or clearly reported as invalid, rather than silently converted to another quantity. It claimed this outcome: Typing 1.5 displayed 15 with Confirm enabled. Confirming generated 15 CODES-VALID-prefixed Draft code rows and showed “Unsaved changes: Codes.”. Review concluded: Human review rejected this report as intended integer input validation, not an issue. The controlled Code Quantity field discards unsupported decimal-point and intermediate-minus keystrokes. Sequentially typing 1.5 visibly leaves 15 before Confirm; typing minus followed by 1 visibly leaves 1. Confirm generates exactly the displayed accepted integer count as local, unsaved Draft codes. This intended behavior should not be flagged as a bug.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Using the authenticated fixture session (the dashboard showed admin@example.com), navigate through Discounts > Vouchers at /discounts/vouchers. Create a fresh voucher named NEGPLN-PCT-20261013-7341 with unique code MOM-PLN-5F8A2D91C63E, assign Channel-PLN, choose Percentage, and save. To create the voucher, use 1% initially; then edit its Discount section, set Channel-PLN to 0, save, reload, and reopen Discount to confirm the saved 0. On the voucher at /discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlOjE0NA%3D, focus the Channel-PLN percentage field, press Control+A, and type -5 using normal keyboard input. Observe that the field displays 5 with no validation, then click Save and verify the “Voucher updated” confirmation and persisted 5% value. The rejected report expected: The negative percentage should be rejected with visible validation and should not be silently converted into a different, positive discount. It claimed this outcome: From a saved Channel-PLN value of 0, normal keyboard entry of -5 displayed 5 without validation. Save succeeded with a “Voucher updated” confirmation, and 5% remained saved. Review concluded: Human review confirmed this is intentional nonnegative discount input formatting, not a bug. A discount percentage cannot be negative: the input filters the minus sign and displays the accepted nonnegative value before Save. Saving that displayed percentage is correct behavior. The reported expectation that a filtered minus keystroke must produce a validation error or prevent saving the displayed valid discount is rejected.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher. Enter a unique voucher name and manual code, assign Channel-USD, choose Entire order and Percentage, and set a valid 10% discount. Enable Minimal order value, type the minus and 1 keys sequentially in the Channel-USD amount field, and press Tab. Observe the displayed 1.00 USD before Save. Click Save, reopen the voucher from the Vouchers list, and confirm Minimal order value remains enabled at 1.00 USD. The rejected report expected: A negative minimum order value should be rejected with visible validation, preventing Save until the value is valid. It claimed this outcome: Typing -1 and blurring displayed 1.00 USD without a validation message. Save succeeded, and the reopened voucher retained Minimal order value enabled at 1.00 USD. Review concluded: Human review confirmed this is intended unsigned monetary input filtering, not a bug. VoucherRequirements uses PriceFieldV2, whose formatter removes the minus sign and displays the accepted positive amount before submission. Save preserves that visible 1.00 USD value; it does not silently change a submitted negative amount. This rejection covers the reported sequential typing of -1, not an unverified claim that a negative amount reaches storage.

explanation: A form can keep the error from its last Save attempt visible while the user edits a correction, then validate again on the next submission. This pattern matches a report that requires that old server error to disappear immediately on typing or leaving the field, despite review accepting submit-time feedback. If the user restores the already saved values, Save can also become disabled because there is no pending change. Errors or false unsaved warnings remaining after a genuinely successful save are separate failures.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher. Enter a unique voucher name, add a unique manual code, assign Channel-USD, and choose Entire order with Fixed amount. Set the Channel-USD amount to 0 and click Save. Observe “This field is required” and the red outline. Replace 0 with 5 and blur the field. Navigate to Details and back to Discount; observe 5.00 USD while the required-field message and red outline remain. The rejected report expected: After changing the amount to a valid positive value and blurring the field, the required-field error and red outline should clear. It claimed this outcome: Channel-USD displays 5.00 USD but still shows “This field is required” and a red outline after blur and after navigating from Discount to Details and back. Review concluded: This follows the dashboard’s server-submission feedback convention: Customer email and Attribute label errors also remain after correcting and blurring, then clear on the next successful Save. Voucher amount edits update draft values without revalidating the previous server response. The retained message is not a bug; this finding’s clear-on-edit expectation does not apply to these submission errors.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher. Enter a unique name and manual code, assign Channel-PLN, and set a valid 10% entire-order discount. Set Start Date to 01/01/2020 at 09:30 AM and enable an end date of 01/02/2020 at 09:30 AM. Save the voucher. Change the saved end to 01/01/2020 at 08:30 AM and click Save. Observe the end-before-start validation message. Restore the saved end of 01/02/2020 at 09:30 AM and blur. Observe the retained message and disabled Save button. The rejected report expected: After restoring a valid end date and time later than the start, the validation message and invalid field styling should clear without another submission. It claimed this outcome: Save rejected an end of 01/01/2020 at 08:30 AM before a start of 01/01/2020 at 09:30 AM. Restoring the saved end of 01/02/2020 at 09:30 AM left the red End Date outline and “End date cannot be before the start date” message visible after blur. Save was disabled because the restored schedule was unchanged. Review concluded: Human review rejected this as the dashboard’s normal submit-time validation convention. Editing and blurring draft fields do not clear the last server submission error; validation is refreshed by a later submission, and a successful submission clears that feedback. Customer and Attribute forms use the same convention. Restoring the saved schedule makes the form unchanged, so disabling Save is correct and does not indicate a failed save. Retaining this previous error after correction is not a bug. This rejection does not cover stale schedule values or a false Unsaved warning after a successful Save.

explanation: A focused numeric input can increase or decrease when the mouse wheel scrolls over it. This pattern matches a report that remembers the earlier typed number, overlooks the visibly changed draft, and blames Save or refresh for the decrement even though the displayed submitted value is preserved. Check the field immediately before Save and repeat while scrolling outside it. A number first changing during submission, without a prior input interaction, is outside this rejection.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers. Create a disposable voucher with a unique name and manual code, assign Channel-USD, set a valid 10% discount, leave Minimum Requirements disabled, and save. Open the saved voucher, enable Minimum quantity of items, enter 4, and click Save. Refresh the voucher and inspect the enabled quantity field; the report claims it displays 3. The rejected report expected: After saving and refreshing, Minimum quantity of items remains enabled and displays the submitted quantity of 4. It claimed this outcome: The report describes 4 before Save and 3 after refresh, with Minimum quantity of items still enabled. Review concluded: Human review confirmed this is not a bug: scrolling inside the quantity input changed the displayed draft from 4 to 3 before Save. Save and refresh preserved the submitted value rather than decrementing it. Independent UI verification submitted 4, received 4 from the API, and retained 4 after reload. The pinned quantity field is a number input with step 1, and the save handler preserves an integer 4. The separately accepted fractional-input truncation defect does not apply to this report.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: At a 375×812 viewport, open /discounts/vouchers and use the supplied authenticated Admin session. Create a new test-owned voucher named MOMENTIC-CHANNEL-PCT-10-Q7Z9 and add the unique manual code MOCHAN10Q7Z9. Select Entire order and Percentage, and assign only Channel-PLN. Enter 10 in the Channel-PLN percentage field and verify it displays 10 before saving. Save the voucher. On its details page, observe that the Channel-PLN percentage field displays 9. Refresh the details page and inspect the Channel-PLN percentage field again; it still displays 9. The rejected report expected: After saving and refreshing, the Channel-PLN percentage field should still show the entered value of 10%. It claimed this outcome: The field showed 10 before saving, then showed 9 after save and continued to show 9 after refreshing the voucher details page. Review concluded: Human review rejected this finding: scrolling over the focused percentage number input changes the visible draft from 10 to 9 before Save. Scrolling outside the input does not cause the change. Save persists the already displayed 9; it does not reduce a submitted 10. The recording independently shows the user-triggered input change about 6.3 seconds before the Save click. This rejection covers the reported wheel interaction and alleged save-time decrement, not a value changing during Save without prior input interaction or the separately accepted fractional-input and percentage-validation defects.

explanation: A completely blank optional field can deliberately receive a default, such as midnight for an absent start time or the current date when no start date was supplied. This pattern matches a report that calls that documented default loss of an entered value even though nothing was entered in the relevant field. The distinction is between genuinely unset input and visible partial input. Discarding entered date or time components, or failing to display the saved default afterward, remains a separate issue.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher. Enter a unique voucher name and manual code, assign a channel, and set a valid entire-order percentage discount. Choose a future start date and leave Start Hour completely blank (--:--), without entering an hour or minute. Click Save and inspect the Schedule card; the selected date uses 12:00 AM (00:00). The rejected report expected: Leaving Start Hour completely blank should use midnight (00:00, displayed as 12:00 AM) on the selected start date. It claimed this outcome: Saving with a selected start date and a completely blank Start Hour uses midnight on that date. Review concluded: Human review confirmed that a completely blank optional Start Hour correctly defaults to midnight (12:00 AM). The dashboard’s joinDateTime helper explicitly uses 00:00 when time is unset. This rejection applies only when no hour or minute was entered. A partially entered time such as 10:00 -- is a different case: changing its entered hour and minute to midnight is not covered by this rejection.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher. Enter a unique name and manual code, assign Channel-USD, and configure a valid Entire order discount of 10%. Leave Start Date completely blank, with no date segments entered, and click Save. Inspect the saved Schedule and reload the voucher; the default current start date is displayed and retained. The rejected report expected: A genuinely blank Start Date may use the current date and time when the voucher is saved. It claimed this outcome: Creating a voucher with Start Date completely blank succeeds; the saved Schedule displays the current date, which remains present after reload. Review concluded: Human review accepts defaulting a genuinely unset date. The dashboard sends null for an empty date, and the backend start-date field explicitly defaults to the current time. This rejection covers the default itself, not visibly partial date input or the separately accepted edit-form failure to display the saved default.

explanation: A form can correctly refuse invalid input and preserve the saved value without using the reporter's preferred error phrase, extra message or additional red outline. This pattern matches those reviewed feedback preferences when valid corrections work and no applicable requirement for the requested treatment is established. Verify the actual rejection, recovery and saved state rather than judging only the wording. Proven silent refusal, misleading success, an applicable accessibility requirement or inability to recover is outside this narrow rejection.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers. Create and save a disposable voucher with a unique name and manual code, Channel-PLN, and a valid 10% entire-order discount. In Schedule, set Start Date and End Date to June 1, 2030, Start Hour to 10:00 AM and End Hour to 09:30 AM. Click Save. Observe the rejected Save and “End date cannot be before the start date” message beneath End Date. Keep the same dates, change End Hour to 10:30 AM and click Save. Observe successful saving and “Voucher updated.”. The rejected report expected: The rejected report asks for different wording solely because the calendar dates match. No wording change is required: date includes hours, so June 1 at 09:30 is before June 1 at 10:00. This reference does not reject a report identifying missing End Hour error styling. It claimed this outcome: Before Save, both calendar dates are June 1, 2030, with Start Hour 10:00 AM and End Hour 09:30 AM. After Save, the earlier combined timestamp is correctly rejected with “End date cannot be before the start date.” A wording-only report calls this message inaccurate because the calendar dates match; that expectation is rejected. A 10:30 AM end saves successfully. Review concluded: Human review rejected the claim that the date wording is inaccurate. Date includes hours: June 1, 2030 at 09:30 is before June 1, 2030 at 10:00. The backend compares complete DateTime values and correctly rejects this earlier end with “End date cannot be before the start date.” The same-day 10:30 end saves successfully. Both the chronological validation and this wording are acceptable; time-specific wording is not required. This rejection concerns the initial error wording, not stale errors after correction, failed validation, or stale values and dirty state after a successful Save. Missing error styling on End Hour is a separate human-approved severity-1 presentation bug; a finding identifying that omission must not be rejected by this wording-only reference.

explanation: Spreadsheet-style fill-down copies or extends values into other cells, but it still follows each field's supported values and currency precision. This pattern matches a report that expects the operation to apply unsupported cells, such as invalid negative inputs, or preserve extra decimal places that the field deliberately normalizes. A hint that values can be pasted does not promise arbitrary input support. Check valid fill-down controls and the effective cell values before calling skipped invalid cells or supported normalization data loss.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Sign in as the fixture administrator and create a voucher with Channel-PLN and Channel-USD, a fixed amount of 5 for each, and Minimal order value PLN 100.25 / USD 200.75. Paste the two-line text -10.50 and -20.75 into the PLN Minimal order value field after selecting its contents, then blur. Observe PLN 10.50 and USD 200.75 without an error, then Save and reload. The rejected report expected: The reporter expects the pasted column to fill down to USD, or the negative values to be rejected with a validation error. It claimed this outcome: PLN displays 10.50 before Save, USD keeps 200.75, no validation appears, and both values persist after Save and reload. Review concluded: The observed behavior is intended. The spreadsheet column paste skips invalid cells by design, and sanitizeSpreadsheetPrice treats negative values as invalid, so neither row fills down. The browser's ordinary paste then goes through the unsigned monetary formatter, which removes the minus sign, as the existing Negative minimum order value rejection already established. The positive amount is visible before Save, and Save preserves exactly that displayed value. The fill-down hint covers valid amounts and promises nothing about negative cells. The post-run reproducer confirmed the observations, not that they are a defect.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Create a unique DISC-QA voucher with code and PLN/USD channels. Select Products and Fixed amount. Save fixed amounts PLN 31.25 and USD 42.50. Copy a two-line column containing -5 then 22.345, focus the PLN amount and paste. Observe PLN remains 31.25 while USD becomes 22.34; click Save. Observe Voucher updated and reopen the voucher; amounts remain 31.25 and 22.34. The rejected report expected: Invalid or truncated pasted values should be validated with clear user feedback rather than silently skipping a row or truncating precision without notice. It claimed this outcome: Channel-PLN remains unchanged at 31.25 while Channel-USD updates to 22.34 without any validation warning, and saving reports 'Voucher updated' with the values persisting on reload. Review concluded: Works as intended: bulk paste skips invalid cells such as negatives and limits amounts to the currency's decimal places, the same as typing.

explanation: A short badge, selection count or secondary label often summarizes only part of an item's configuration. In the reviewed cases, a discount-type badge did not promise to show its amount, a selection count did not display both numeric bounds, or a shortened secondary label did not replace the full identity shown elsewhere. This pattern matches an inference of lost or wrong data from that abbreviated text while the full configuration and actual operation remain correct. Verify the detailed value or selected object before deciding that the summary proves corruption.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Create a voucher with a unique manual code, only Channel-PLN, Entire order and Percentage 10. Save and reload. Compare the Entire order · % header pill with the 10% channel value. The rejected report expected: The reporter expects the header pill to include the configured percentage. It claimed this outcome: The header pill shows Entire order · % while the Channel-PLN field shows 10. Review concluded: Intended. The header pill labels the voucher's scope and discount type, not its amount: getVoucherTypePillLabel renders scope plus % or Fixed, and its unit test expects exactly Entire order · %. Percentages can differ by channel and are shown in the Discount section. The post-run reproducer reached the same conclusion.

explanation: A minimum purchase or item-count requirement of zero imposes no minimum: every otherwise eligible purchase satisfies it. This pattern matches a report that treats saving that zero as the same semantic state as turning the requirement off as loss of a meaningful restriction. The reviewed equivalence is specific to these minimum thresholds. It does not justify discarding a positive requirement, treating every zero-valued control as disabled, or giving misleading success feedback for a rejected edit.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Create a fresh unique REQ-QA voucher with Channel-PLN and a 10% entire-order discount. Enable Minimal order value and save a positive amount such as 12.34 PLN. Change the enabled amount to 0, blur, and click Save. After Voucher updated, refresh and scroll to Minimum Requirements. The rejected report expected: Saving should be blocked while an 'Invalid minimum spend' error is present, or the zero amount should be handled with clear feedback. It claimed this outcome: Save completes successfully with a checkmark, but reloading the voucher shows the Minimal order value toggle switched off. Review concluded: Works as intended: a minimum order value of 0 means no minimum, so the requirement shows as off after saving.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Assign Channel-PLN and Channel-USD; set both percentage discounts to 10%. Enable minimal order value with 100.25 PLN and 25.50 USD and save. Open Requirements; set PLN minimum to 0 and save, then reload. Switch to Minimum quantity of items, enter 0 and blur. Observe “Enter at least 1 item.”. Click Save, allow the update to settle, and reload the voucher's Requirements. The rejected report expected: The displayed minimum-one-item validation prevents saving 0, retaining the invalid input for correction and the previous saved configuration. It claimed this outcome: Save removes the quantity input and disables both minimum modes; this persists after reload. A whole-page assertion confirmed no validation error remained and Save was disabled. Review concluded: Works as intended: the field says to enter at least 1 item; a minimum of 0 means no minimum requirement, as with vouchers-b08.

explanation: A value required when an item is used need not be required at every earlier setup stage. The reviewed examples allow an unfinished discount to be saved, a required query input to have no saved default, or an automated action to reach activation before its missing or invalid value is rejected during execution. This pattern matches a report that assumes Save or Active guarantees complete validation at that earlier stage without an applicable requirement. Lost valid inputs, concealed broken references or failure of a complete supported configuration remain independent claims.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: As the administrator, create a fresh ELIG-QA-* voucher with a manual code, both available channels and 10% discount for each channel; save. Select Products under What the voucher discounts. Leave categories, collections and products/variants unassigned and click Save. The rejected report expected: Saving is blocked with validation feedback until at least one category, collection, product, or variant is assigned. It claimed this outcome: The voucher saves successfully with a 'Voucher updated' notification and updates the header badge to 'Products · %' with all assignment groups remaining empty. Review concluded: Works as intended: the edit page deliberately lets a voucher be saved before setup is finished and tracks the missing catalogue as a pending "Required to redeem" step ("Finish them now or come back later"). An empty catalogue doesn't apply to any line items, so nothing is corrupted.

explanation: When the same saved item is open in two tabs, one tab can be editing an older copy of its settings. Under the reviewed last-write-wins contract, saving that older copy may replace another tab's changes rather than merge the two edits or display a conflict warning. This pattern matches a report that assumes merging or conflict detection is guaranteed, despite the submitted older copy explaining the overwrite. A promised conflict-protection feature failing, or data disappearing without a competing save, is outside this rejection.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: As Maya staff, create a unique QA-MULTI voucher with one code, entire-order percentage discount and Channel-PLN assigned; save it. Open its detail in tab A with name QA-MULTI-MAYA-0723-JORDAN and percentage 17. Open the same voucher in tab B, rename to QA-MULTI-MAYA-0723-TAB2, save and refresh to confirm persistence. Switch back to tab A without refreshing. Confirm it still shows the original name and 17%. Change only Channel-PLN percentage to 23 and Save. Refresh tab A and inspect saved name and percentage. The rejected report expected: Saving a distinct discount field should preserve the newer saved voucher name, or show a conflict requiring resolution rather than silently losing the rename. It claimed this outcome: Save showed Voucher updated; after refresh the name had reverted to QA-MULTI-MAYA-0723-JORDAN and percentage was 23. Review concluded: Works as intended: saving from a stale tab overwrites a newer concurrent edit, which is last-write-wins. Like Metabase's concurrent-edit labels, the app isn't expected to merge or detect conflicting saves.

explanation: A form's unsaved-changes warning can mean that the user has edited the form since opening it, rather than that its current values differ from the saved values. This pattern matches a report that changes a value, types the original value back, and assumes the warning must disappear despite review accepting the first policy. The warning alone does not show that data was changed or lost. Establish the form's actual warning policy and distinguish it from a warning that remains after a confirmed successful save.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: As administrator, open a fresh Create Voucher form with no prerequisites or settings edited. Enter EDIT-newdraft-undo in Voucher Name. Select all text in Voucher Name, press Backspace and blur the field. Click Back in the bottom action bar. The rejected report expected: After restoring the edited Voucher Name field to its initial blank state, clicking Back navigates back without an unsaved changes warning. It claimed this outcome: A 'Leave without saving changes?' confirmation dialog appears upon clicking Back. Review concluded: Works as intended: the unsaved-changes warning tracks whether the form was edited, not whether it returns to its original values, so typing and clearing a name still warns.

explanation: The report describes a failure, but independent review did not recover the claimed failing state under the stated conditions. This group records that evidence limitation rather than an established explanation of why the behavior was correct or why the original event occurred. A future report must match the same trigger and outcome and still needs its own reliable reproduction; resemblance to a nearby accepted bug is insufficient. Nonreproduction does not prove the event impossible or intended.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Create and save a disposable QA-GENCODES voucher with generated codes, Channel-USD and 10% discount. Choose Add code > Generate codes. Paste -1 into Code Quantity (max 50). Click enabled Confirm. Observe unchanged voucher codes table and feedback. The rejected report expected: A negative code count is rejected with disabled Confirm or a clear validation message, retaining the dialog for correction. It claimed this outcome: Confirm is enabled for -1, closes the dialog, leaves original codes unchanged, and shows no error or validation anywhere. Whole-page assertion confirmed the missing feedback. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: At 1440 × 900, open Vouchers as the authenticated admin and create a fresh private QA-RESP voucher with one manual code, Channel-USD availability, Entire order percentage 10, and a matching name. Save. Resize to 768 × 900 and scroll to Percentage for Channel-USD. Replace 10 with 12. In the observed run the keyboard entry displayed 112; replace that entire value with 12 and verify it displays 12. Scroll to the bottom and click Save. Observe the Voucher updated confirmation. Refresh, wait for the voucher to load, and scroll to the Channel-USD percentage. The rejected report expected: The saved percentage should equal the displayed 12%. It claimed this outcome: The refreshed Channel-USD input shows 11%, not the displayed 12% that was saved. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: Create a fresh QA-REQ Free shipping voucher with unique code and Channel-USD assigned. Enable Minimal order value and enter 20.25 USD. Save. Clear the USD value, blur, click Save and wait at least 3 seconds. Observe Voucher updated and Unsaved changes: Channels together. Reload and open Requirements without editing. The rejected report expected: After successfully saving the voucher with a cleared minimum order value, the unsaved changes state should clear and the Save button should disable (or, if a blank value is disallowed, display a validation error rather than a success notification). It claimed this outcome: A “Voucher updated” notification appears, yet “Unsaved changes: Channels” remains in the footer and the Save button stays enabled. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Saleor, follow this workflow: As admin open Percentage order discount. Set PLN percentage to 7.5, save, then change scope to Products and save. Change scope to Entire order, enter 5 in Channel-PLN percentage, then Save. Reload and inspect Discount. The rejected report expected: Channel-PLN percentage input should accept the entered value (5%) and persist it after save and reload. It claimed this outcome: Channel-PLN percentage immediately reverts to 75% upon typing and remains 75% after saving and reloading. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

explanation: A script can inject a field value that an ordinary user cannot enter through the supported form. This pattern matches a claimed user-interface reproduction where both typing and pasting are blocked, and the failing state appears only after the script bypasses those controls. It does not establish that the normal interface accepts that invalid input. Use a real supported input path before filing the UI claim; backend validation or a separately reachable failure remains a different question.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Create fresh DISC-prefixed voucher with unique manual code, Channel-USD and Free shipping, then Save. Enable Minimal order value, enter 2 USD and Save successfully. Enable Minimum quantity of items and enter -1. Save and inspect the requirements section. The rejected report expected: Saving should be rejected with a visible field validation error while retaining the enabled control and entered value so the user can correct it. It claimed this outcome: A “Couldn't save voucher” toast directs the user to check highlighted fields, but both minimum requirement toggles turn off and the quantity input field disappears, leaving no highlighted field visible to correct. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce through the UI: the minimum-quantity field blocks typing or pasting a minus sign, so a negative quantity can only be set programmatically.

explanation: When daylight-saving time moves clocks forward, some local wall-clock times do not occur in that timezone. This pattern matches a report that enters a schedule time inside that missing interval and calls normalization to the next valid hour loss of an existing valid time. Check the chosen date, timezone and clock transition before demanding an identical round trip. A valid local time changing incorrectly, or an existing instant being shifted under the wrong timezone, is a different failure.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: Browser timezone America/Los_Angeles, desktop 1920x1080. Original observation used an already saved own fixture; verification should create a fresh fixture as described. Open Vouchers as the supplied admin and click Create voucher. Create a fresh uniquely named TIME-prefixed voucher. Add a unique manual code, assign Channel-USD using Availability Manage, and enter a 10% entire-order discount. Set Start Date to March 14, 2027 and Start Hour to 02:30 AM. Enable Set end date and set End Date March 14, 2027, End Hour 04:00 AM. Verify entered fields before saving. Click Save and inspect Start Hour and feedback. Reload the saved voucher and inspect Start Hour again. The rejected report expected: If the entered local time cannot occur due to daylight saving, explain and reject it or request correction rather than silently saving a different hour. It claimed this outcome: Start Hour changes from 02:30 AM to 03:30 AM after Save and remains 03:30 AM after reload. Default multimodal assertion confirmed no warning or validation message anywhere explaining the change. Review concluded: Works as intended: 02:30 AM on March 14, 2027 does not exist in America/Los_Angeles (clocks jump from 2:00 to 3:00), so it resolves to 03:30 AM, the same instant.

explanation: These reports were rejected by a reviewer as intended behavior, but the record does not explain why. This is a holding group, not an established reusable explanation of what the model misunderstood. A new report can be compared with the exact rejected action and outcome in the example, but similar wording alone is insufficient to declare it intended. Recover the missing rationale or obtain new evidence before applying a more specific rejection rule.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: As vouchers admin, create a fresh QA-DISCOUNT voucher with a unique manual code and PLN/USD availability; save valid percentage values. Open Discount and switch to Fixed amount. Enter -1 for Channel-PLN and 12.345 for Channel-USD. Save, refresh, and reopen Discount. The rejected report expected: Reject a negative discount with understandable validation rather than silently converting it to a positive discount. It claimed this outcome: The saved and refreshed voucher shows 1.00 PLN. USD also shows 12.34 after entering 12.345. A whole-page multimodal assertion confirmed no error or rounding warning appeared. Review concluded: Works as intended per human review.

explanation: A Saleor voucher is a discount configuration containing one or more redeemable codes, and its internal name can be optional. In the reviewed case, a blank or whitespace-only name was allowed and the list could show a fallback such as the number of codes instead of exposing a specific code in that cell. This pattern matches an assumption that the name must be rejected or that the cell must become a complete visible identifier. It does not establish that codes were lost, nor settle a different failure to open or identify the correct saved voucher.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, follow this workflow: As authenticated admin, create a fresh voucher with unique NAME-prefixed code and NAME-prefixed name, one available channel and entire-order 10% discount; save. Change Voucher Name to exactly three ordinary spaces and Save. Verify Voucher updated appears, then refresh and use Back to return to All vouchers. Inspect the voucher's Name cell. The rejected report expected: A whitespace-only name should be treated as unnamed and show an identifying fallback (such as its code), or be rejected with validation rather than producing an unidentified list row. It claimed this outcome: Save succeeds. After refresh and Back, the voucher row's Name cell shows only “1 code”; neither the voucher name nor its code is displayed. Review concluded: Works as intended: voucher name is optional (internal staff name), so a whitespace-only name is treated as unnamed and the row falls back to the code count.

explanation: A menu, panel or narrow text field may show only part of its contents until the user scrolls, moves within the field or copies the complete value. This pattern matches a report that calls an option or value missing or incorrect from that initial visible slice, while the reviewed normal interaction reveals it in full and the control works. Inspect the complete content before alleging loss. Essential information that remains inaccessible through the supported interaction is a different failure.
reproductionPaths: At phone width in a Saleor voucher’s codes table, generated codes sharing a prefix can be truncated to identical-looking text, without an inline expansion or horizontal-scroll reveal. Review accepted this display because each full code can still be copied. This rejects treating that copyable truncation alone as an eligible unavailable-identifier defect; it does not establish that the text expands on tap, or reject an incorrect/missing copied value.
